requirement:
A record MUST be changed only if every rewrite a mapping calls for in it
verifies under {cite}`requirements.refactor.outline_inputs`,
{cite}`requirements.refactor.definition_inputs`,
{cite}`requirements.refactor.subject_text`, and
{cite}`requirements.refactor.reference_digest`; otherwise the whole record MUST
be left unchanged and reported with the check that failed. Records that no
mapping affects MUST be left byte-identical.
rationale:
**Verdict:** the implementation looks complete, but the tests for `requirements.refactor.whole_record` leave obligations unverified.

**Implementation (no gap found).**
- `src/refactor.rs#fn[rewrite_record]` carries the all-or-nothing rule. It collects every failed check into `failures` and returns `Outcome::Unchanged(failures.join("; "))` if any exist. Nothing is written for such a record, and `refactor` reports the reason in the "records unchanged" list. This covers "otherwise the whole record MUST be left unchanged and reported with the check that failed".
- A record is changed only when all four checks pass:
  - outline inputs: `fn[rewrite_input]` compares the mapped-back hash with the recorded hash;
  - requirements and definition inputs: `fn[rewrite_input]` compares the mapped-back text and the mapped matches;
  - subject text: the `requirement`/`example` field is rewritten only if the mapped-back body equals the recorded body, otherwise a "text of … changed" failure is pushed;
  - reference digest: `States::digests` is compared with the recorded digest, otherwise a failure is pushed.
- Unaffected records return `Outcome::Unaffected` and are never written.

**Tests (gaps).**
- Only two tests carry `{test}` for this requirement: `tests/refactor.rs#fn[a_moved_function_keeps_its_evidence_current]` and `tests/refactor.rs#fn[a_function_edited_while_moving_leaves_its_records_stale]`.
- The failure test exercises only one failing check, the outline-input hash. It asserts that the record stays byte-identical and that the report names `inputs[1]` and the check.
- No test tagged for `whole_record` makes the subject-text check or the reference-digest check fail. I found no test anywhere that edits a definition body or a reference set so that these checks refuse a rewrite. The definition-input refusal appears in `fn[a_moved_requirement_renames_its_references_and_evidence]`, but that test is not tagged for this requirement.
- No test tagged for `whole_record` shows that one failing check blocks other rewrites the record would otherwise get. In the tagged failure test, nothing else in the record would have been rewritten except the rationale. The only nearby case, `rules.check` in the moved-requirement test, is not tagged for this requirement.
- The success test checks only that `rules.check` is absent from the report. No test asserts that a record no mapping affects is byte-identical. `snapshot` is used only in the dry-run and invalid-mapping tests, which are not tagged for this requirement.

These untested failure and byte-identity obligations are unacknowledged gaps; no `{fixme}` covers them.
